extracted.intended_audience: journalists, scientists, and press officers (primarily UK national science/news outlets)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how journalists, scientists and press officers can work with the Science Media Centre to access expertise, run briefings, and receive media-training and support for science/health/environment stories. Covers the Centre’s services, target audiences, and the kinds of assistance it provides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate scientist engagement to improve public access to evidence-based information
rubrics_metrics.description: Our ultimate goal is to facilitate more scientists to engage with the media, in the hope that the public will have improved access to accurate, evidence-based scientific information about the stories of the day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide journalists what they need in the timeframe they need
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science Media Centre provides journalists with what they need in the timeframe they need it, from interviews with leading experts to timely press briefings on topical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: arranging interviews with leading experts; organising timely press briefings on topical issues — emphasis on responsiveness and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give journalists access to information, best evidence and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide journalists with information about science and its related disciplines, making it easier for them to get access to the best evidence and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied standard: ensure accuracy and evidence-based sourcing; curate access to subject-matter experts and reliable scientific material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus services on science in the headlines and national news outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Given our focus on science in the headlines, the SMC works mainly with science and news journalists in the UK’s national news outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience/eligibility note: primary engagement is with UK national science and news media rather than local or niche outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help scientists, engineers and experts engage with the media and be heard
rubrics_metrics.description: We work with scientists, engineers and other experts, helping them engage with the media and creating more opportunities for them to get their voices heard on the big science, health and environment stories of the day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service emphasis: creating opportunities for expert voices on major topical stories; support aimed at enabling public communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run events and provide guidelines and top tips on media work
rubrics_metrics.description: The SMC also runs regular events to introduce experts to what media work involves, and provides guidelines and top tips on media work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formats include regular introductory events/training and written guidelines/top tips — implies expectation that experts attend or consult these resources to prepare for media engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work closely with press officers from universities, industry and funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Primarily a press office, the Science Media Centre works closely with press officers from universities, industry, research funders, and other leading science and engineering institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative role: liaison and partnership with institutional press officers to coordinate coverage and messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support complex stories by providing advice and an independent neutral venue
rubrics_metrics.description: We support them when they are working on complex science, health and environment stories, providing advice and an independent neutral venue where the science and engineering communities can come together to speak out on issues of major concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services for complex issues include advisory support and hosting neutral briefings or events to convene multiple experts and stakeholders; emphasis on independence and neutrality.
